title: Taiwan's chipmaker TSMC explores collaborating with Elon Musks's Terafab complex in Texas
key_facts: TSMC posted record July-September net profit of NT$763.1 billion (nearly $24 billion), up 69% on the year; revenue was NT$1.49 trillion ($46 billion), up 51%.
C.C. Wei, TSMC chairman and CEO, said on the earnings call the company is open to working with Elon Musk's planned Terafab chip complex in Texas and 'is in discussions to be part of' it.
Wei stressed that any Texas plant 'must be run by TSMC'; the plan is still under deliberation and teams were sent to Texas to evaluate it.
Musk said on X earlier this month that talks with TSMC took place but 'we will build and run the fab', with TSMC at most subleasing part of Terafab.
TSMC has pledged $265 billion for Arizona plants and raised its 2026 capital spending budget to $60-64 billion from $52-56 billion.
Wei said demand is far above what TSMC can supply, but warned price-sensitive consumer markets are being challenged and that TSMC is prudent about 2027.
quote_evidence: TSMC is in discussions to be part of the "Terafab" project in Texas, Wei added, stressing that a plant in Texas must be run by TSMC.
Musk confirmed on X earlier this month that there have been discussions with TSMC over its potential role in Terafab, but he also said "we will build and run the fab,"
why_it_matters_hint: Terafab could add a new US source of advanced chips, but TSMC and Musk disagree on who runs it.
notes: Read in full via Fortune. Livemint and BigGo transcript confirm Wei's wording.
